PullRequest.Title: sessions: let remote message recipients reply to the exact sender
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349566

When a chat receives a message through `send_remote_message`, it had no way to reply to the exact chat that sent it. `get_current_session` and `get_session_context` did not show a sender, and `session: "origin"` only addresses the chat that created the session. Messages already carry the sender in their delegation metadata (`vscode.chat.delegation`), so this change exposes it without changing the host protocol.

## Changes

- **`send_remote_message` accepts `session: "sender"`.** It replies to the chat whose message started the calling chat's current turn. The address is read from that turn's message, so a later message from another chat cannot redirect the reply. A sender on the same host is mapped to its host-qualified session. If the current turn was not started by another chat, the call fails with an error.
- **`get_session_context` reports `from: { chat, replyWith }` for each agent-sent turn.** `chat` is an exact reference to the sending chat, including nested chats. `replyWith` names the tool that accepts it: `send_message` for a sender on the same host, `send_remote_message` otherwise. Because the sender is reported per turn, a later turn can still reply to an earlier sender, as in the A → B → C → B → A chain.
- `readAgentMessageSender` only reads agent- or tool-authored messages, and reuses the address validation that `origin` already uses. It does not use prompt text or other `_meta` fields.
- The sender reference is only an address. Replies still go through the existing resolution, approval and workspace-trust checks, and `origin` behaves as before.
- Updated the model-facing tool descriptions and the Remote delegation section of `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reply to the current turn's exact sender using send_remote_message, including nested and same-host senders; preserve explicit-target and origin sends.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool preparation resolves the source session, reads the current chat only for the new sender alias, and resolves the target before approval. Invocation repeats resolution, then waits for target state, workspace trust, background client-tool preparation, dispatch, and acknowledgement. Explicit targets and origin bypass the added source-chat read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition per resolution, normally warm; at most one subscribe request per cold resource acquisition, shared while in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source-session resolution and temporary subscription already ran for all remote sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before target resolution in both preparation and invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source Chat state to obtain activeTurn.message delegation metadata; on a cold acquisition subscribe and receive a snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reference per sender resolution, zero added wire requests when held state is available. At most one snapshot per cold resolution, shared by simultaneous holders; relay snapshots use the existing paged chat view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no sender alias or source-chat lookup. Explicit-target and origin sends still perform no such lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Added before approval and sending only for session: sender; cold lookup waits for state with a ten-second cancellation bound.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Determine whether a linked destination chat is its advertised default, using held session state or a host listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero listing calls when destination session state is held; otherwise one listing for the destination reference with a fragment, not one per listed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing explicit links and origin references already used this lookup; the new sender alias yields a reference for the same resolver.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read destination Session and Chat state, prepare client tools through the existing background chat model, and dispatch one queued message with acknowledgement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination session and chat acquisition per actual delivery, with shared warm subscriptions; one message dispatch. Existing background model acquisition is reused when loaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same destination reads, model preparation, dispatch, and acknowledgement were already required for remote sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before successful delivery; destination turns themselves execute after queue admission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve target trust roots and check trust; remote or virtual URI canonicalization may invoke a resolver/provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existing trust passes per delivery. Each checks the target's working directories and related repository/worktree roots, using Promise.all within groups; ordinary agent-host URIs are normalized locally and resolved virtual sources are cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both trust passes and any transitive canonicalization were already on the remote-send path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before background preparation and again before dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source chat and one destination per distinct tool request, including each hop in a delegation chain. Cold snapshot bytes depend on that chat's history; this is not a read per historical turn or per connected session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sender resolution precedes the existing per-target SequencerByKey and send limiter. Concurrent acquisitions for one source share its subscription; different resources remain independent. Destination delivery is serialized per target chat, not globally. This diff adds no loop over destinations or sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentSubscriptionManager shares both hydrated and in-flight subscriptions by resource. Current-turn client tools run through AgentHostSessionHandler, which holds default or additional chat subscriptions; background remote chats also retain models during active work. Thus the normal sender lookup reuses state without a wire read. An unheld or errored source subscription can require one snapshot per resolution, potentially two across preparation and invocation when no other owner retains it. The new reference, timer, and cancellation source are disposed in finally. send() shares in-flight and settled results for the same source/request ID within its existing retry window.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the routing branches, subscription manager's refcount/in-flight behavior, client-tool invocation path, and finally cleanup. The only added boundary is conditional source-chat subscription acquisition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold source-state lookup duration and snapshot sizes were not measured. Ordinary current-turn tool execution has held chat state; no evidence establishes repeated cold transcript transfers on that normal path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added lookup implements the new alias, normally reads already-held state, has constant resource cardinality and balanced cleanup, and does not change existing target/origin send costs. A speculative full-history read per reply would ignore subscription sharing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read get_session_context to find sender addresses for recent or earlier agent-authored turns.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing session listing, target-session restore, and exact-chat state resolution complete before bounded transcript serialization. The added sender parser/link builder runs only for the selected transcript window; response-page requests retain their existing separate serialization path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate the registry and read session catalog metadata; ineligible rows can use provider metadata and persisted session-state fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical listing per context request, shared for overlapping callers; bulk catalog read for the eligible collection, grouped provider prewarming, and fallback only for ineligible sessions with concurrency four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical listing and fallback machinery ran before context reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Listing must finish before resolving context arguments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the requested session and materialize the requested chat/provider backing and history when not already hydrated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One requested session and one requested chat, coalesced per key. Cold peer materialization can read persisted provider data, draft, provider history, and local turns; hydrated chat state avoids materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same restore, history, and persistence reads supplied the same snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to obtain the snapshot before serialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse recognized delegation address metadata, encode an exact sender link, and include from in the existing JSON payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one sender link per selected agent/tool-authored turn; default ten entries, maximum fifty on the production tool path. User-authored turns return without URI parsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded transcript was serialized without sender address fields; assistant text processing and final JSON serialization already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small bounded addition to existing model-facing payload construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Default ten transcript entries, capped at fifty through getSessionContextArgs. Added work scales with selected agent/tool-authored entries and their session/chat address lengths, not all history or all sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing listing legacy fallback is limited to four concurrent sessions, with provider prewarming grouped by provider. Session and chat restores coalesce per resource. Added window serialization is synchronous and bounded, with no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session listing shares concurrent computations by mode/registry epoch and clears settled entries; catalog metadata is read in bulk, with legacy fallback as needed. restoreSession joins per-session restores and uses live state when available. resolveChatState returns hydrated state or joins entry.inFlight. Sender metadata needs no additional lookup or cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff adds only metadata parsing and link construction after entries.slice(windowStart), and the fifty-entry cap is enforced by the production argument parser. No new provider or persistence read is needed to discover senders.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Address sizes and usage frequency were not profiled. Ordinary generated session/chat identifiers are small; no realistic unbounded-address trigger was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added serialization is bounded address metadata, not an additional history scan, restore, or per-turn service call. Existing collection-wide history preparation is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reply to a same-host sender's exact chat through send_message, including a recorded default chat absent from a stale listing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing listSessions resolves a known session. The changed branch compares the linked chat to the recorded default; it then uses that exact default or the existing linked-chat resolver. Existing queued send restores the destination if necessary and starts or enqueues its prompt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read known session metadata through the existing shared listing/catalog path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical listing per send, with the same shared/bulk reads and four-way legacy fallback as the context scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every send already listed sessions before getSendMessageArgs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore an unhydrated destination, then enqueue a message or start its prompt through the existing provider/persistence pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination per queued send; restore only if destination ChatState is absent, followed by one queue admission or prompt start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Known exact linked targets already took this restore/queue/start path with the same cardinality. Newly accepted recorded-default targets now use that existing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs inside the existing per-chat send sequencer before the tool returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One linked target per send. Existing session/chat lookup can scan known metadata, but the added recorded-default lookup is an in-memory lookup; no new loop or destination fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing SequencerByKey serializes queued sends by exact destination chat; different chats remain independent. The changed argument resolver performs no concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getDefaultChat reads live session entries, eviction records, or surfaced summaries synchronously. Existing session listing coalescing and target restore/hydrated-state reuse are unchanged. No new cache or retained state was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced getDefaultChat through agentHostChatOwnershipService to agentHostStateManager's in-memory entries; the added branch does not load or enumerate storage.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime timings. The only additional resolver work is a recorded-default lookup and, when matched, parsing its URI.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Exact-chat resolution changes acceptance semantics without introducing an expensive boundary, increasing send multiplicity, or changing serialization/concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all eight changed files and every diff page against base ce997d62c79464a0c070c3d2654198f0391e1809. Traced sender routing, bounded context serialization, same-host target resolution, shared subscriptions, cleanup, delivery sequencing, listing fallbacks, restore coalescing, and trust boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix identified. Static read-only review; no runtime measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
